citations.assessment: The Tosafot argues from Menahem’s replacement, alongside the Mishnah and its discussion of the pairs. The Bavli records a competing office assignment for Yehudah ben Tabbai and Shimon ben Shataḥ.

Tosafot says Shammai personally agreed with the first members of three pairs, and that the text therefore puts Shammai first. Heilprin uses the school siglum in the first clause and the personal name in the next. Preserve that wording and clarify the referent of the pronoun.
Exact checked gloss presents Shammai’s ordering as the reason for the subsequent ordering convention.
Heilprin’s internal discussion connects the practice with humility. Eruvin describes the practice of Beit Hillel as a school.
The Hillel article explicitly distinguishes the pupil phase from the pupil-colleague phase. This is Heilprin’s reading, not a verified chronology.
Exact tradition transmits Shammai the Elder in Haggai’s name. Heilprin’s comparison of lifespans remains his inference.
The Hillel entry and Rav Huna’s statement identify three disputes between the individual figures. The later schools are distinct.
Heilprin gives the character commendation to Shammai. In the Bavli the devotion formula is applied to Hillel, the personal Shabbat preparation to Shammai and the first-day maxim to Beit Shammai.
The English supplied an implicit “for Heaven.” Translate וכן מחלוקתו directly. The Bavli specifies his staff and satchel, but Heilprin mentions only the staff.
Sukkah counts Hillel’s eighty and explicitly names Yonatan and Rabban Yoḥanan. The inference that all also studied under Shammai is Heilprin’s.
The Mishnah expressly identifies Rabban Yoḥanan as receiving from both. This particular case does not establish the universal pupil claim.
Exact passage frames this as the state of affairs on that day. Textual evidence supports reading לפני behind the printed לכני. Preserve the Hebrew and the localized scene.
Tosafot draws the Elijah rule from Avodah Zarah and adduces the killing account from Yerushalmi Shabbat. Heilprin compresses the two dependencies.

notes.text: Beitzah 16a describes Shammai’s Shabbat preparation. It attributes “all his deeds were for Heaven’s sake” to Hillel and gives the first-day maxim in the name of Beit Shammai. Heilprin’s wording is preserved.
The Mishnah identifies Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai as receiving from both teachers. Heilprin uses this to infer that their entire student body was shared.
Shabbat 17a describes Hillel’s posture on that particular day. The pinned Hebrew’s לכני is read as לפני in translation.
Tosafot cites the Bavli for the Elijah rule and the Yerushalmi for the account of the pupils. The two source attributions are distinct.

Yuhasin gives two prophecies. It places Menahem’s in Herod’s childhood and Shammai’s during Herod’s appearance before the Sanhedrin. Heilprin combines the Shammai attribution with the childhood setting.

The introduction attributed to Shemuel Ha-Nagid counts three rulings as Beit Shammai, distinct from six cases where the Sages agree with neither school. This is separate from the six rulings attributed to Rav Amram.
